about.teamDesc: Die Direktoren und Guides von Aardvark Safaris in Tansania sind engagierte Fachleute mit umfangreicher Erfahrung im Bereich Wildtier-Safaris. Viele haben ihre gesamte Karriere bei uns verbracht und verschiedene Tourismusausbildungen sowie das College of Wildlife Management absolviert. Unsere Guides sind Experten für Flora und Fauna Tansanias und bieten aufschlussreiche Vorträge und individuelle Safari-Erlebnisse. Mit ihrem fundierten Wissen über afrikanische Ökologie, Geschichte und lokale Folklore bieten unsere Guides ein bereicherndes und unvergessliches Safari-Erlebnis.

team.name: Augustine Mwangotya
team.bio: Augustine Mwangotya, Gründer von Aardvark Safaris, wuchs in der Nähe des Kilimandscharo auf und studierte Wildtiermanagement in Tansania. Er arbeitete für das Tanzania Wildlife Department und als Fahrer-Guide für große Reiseunternehmen. Augustine erwarb einen Master-Abschluss am Prescott College mit einer Abschlussarbeit über gemeindebasierte Naturschutzarbeit. Er hat Safaris für Organisationen wie National Geographic und das Jane Goodall Institute geleitet. Augustine ist bekannt für sein Wissen, seine Erzählkunst und seine logistische Expertise. Er ist zudem Philanthrop und unterstützt Waiseneinrichtungen in Arusha, Tansania.

team.name: Walt Anderson
team.bio: Walt Anderson war 27 Jahre lang Professor für Umweltwissenschaften am Prescott College in Arizona und lehrte Naturkunde, Ökologie, Wildtiermanagement, Naturschutz, Ökotourismus sowie Naturkunst und -fotografie. Er ist Signature Artist bei Artists for Conservation, und seine Tiermalereien sind hoch anerkannt. Als erfahrener Naturforscher, bekannt für seinen Enthusiasmus und Humor, ist er seit seiner ersten ostafrikanischen Safari 1979 ein versierter Guide und Interpret der regionalen Tierwelt. Er war Gründungsvorsitzender des Vorstands des Biocultural Conservation Institute. Inzwischen im Ruhestand vom aktiven Safari-Guiding, vertritt Anderson Aardvark Tanzania in den USA und unterstützt die Organisation von Safari-Arrangements.

team.name: Deborah Mrema
team.bio: Mit umfassender Kenntnis der afrikanischen Safari aus eigener Erfahrung in Ostafrika versprechen Deborah und ihr Team Ihnen ein einmaliges Erlebnis in Afrikas landschaftlich schönsten und wunderbarsten Reisezielen. Im Herzen jedes Abenteuers, das Sie mit Aardvark Safaris wählen, geben Sie dem Erlebnis Leben und Sinn. Überlassen Sie es uns, dafür zu sorgen, dass es ein Schatz fürs Leben wird!

experiences.whenDesc: Die beste Reisezeit für Tansania hängt von Ihren individuellen Interessen und geplanten Aktivitäten ab. Ob Wildtierbeobachtung, Bergabenteuer, kulturelles Eintauchen oder ein entspannter Strandurlaub — Tansania bietet das ganze Jahr über etwas für jeden Reisenden.

seasons.title: Trockenzeit (Juni bis Oktober)
items: Beste Zeit für Wildtierbeobachtungen — Tiere versammeln sich an Flüssen und Wasserstellen.
Klarer Himmel und trockene Bedingungen machen sie zur bevorzugten Zeit für die Besteigung des Kilimandscharo.

seasons.title: Grüne Saison (November bis Mai)
items: Ideal für Vogelbeobachtung — Zugvögel strömen in dieser Zeit nach Tansania.
Weniger Touristen als in der Trockenzeit — ruhigere und günstigere Erlebnisse.
Üppige Vegetation und wunderschöne Landschaften in den nördlichen Parks.
Einzigartige Fotomöglichkeiten mit lebhaften Farben und dramatischen Wolkenformationen.

seasons.title: Übergangssaison (März–Mai & November)
items: Ein Gleichgewicht zwischen Trocken- und Grünzeit mit weniger Touristen.
Unterkunfts- und Tourpreise können günstiger sein.
Kühlere Temperaturen bieten angenehme Bedingungen für Aktivitäten im Freien.

circuits.intro: After the dust of the bush, Tanzania's coast is the classic finale — UNESCO Stone Town, spice plantations, dhow sails at sunset, and reef islands where whale sharks gather off Mafia and Pemba's walls drop into turquoise water. posts.title: Wann Sie die Große Migration erleben können
posts.excerpt: Ein Monat-für-Monat-Leitfaden — wo die Herden sind, wo die Raubtiere warten und wie Sie Ihren Besuch für die Flussüberquerungen planen.
body: Die Große Migration ist kein einzelnes Ereignis — sie ist ein ganzjähriger, 800 Kilometer langer Kreislauf des Lebens, der zwischen der südlichen Serengeti Tansanias und Kenias Maasai Mara verläuft. Zu wissen, wo die Herden sich in einem bestimmten Monat befinden, macht den Unterschied zwischen dem stillen Grasen tausender Gnus und dem Miterleben einer hunderttausend Tiere starken Flussüberquerung.

Von Ende Januar bis März versammeln sich die Herden auf den Kurzgrasebenen rund um Ndutu und die südliche Serengeti. Dies ist die Kalbungszeit — etwa 8.000 Kälber werden täglich über einen Zeitraum von rund drei Wochen geboren. Raubtiere sind allgegenwärtig: Geparden auf den offenen Ebenen, Löwen an den Sümpfen und Hyänen an den Rändern. Für Erstbesucher und Fotografen ist dies wohl das lohnendste Zeitfenster des Jahres.

April und Mai bringen den großen Regen, und die Herden beginnen sich nord- und westwärts zu bewegen, in Richtung des Westkorridors. Die Touristenzahlen sinken, die Preise fallen und die Landschaft erstrahlt in elektrischem Grün. Bis Juni und Anfang Juli erreichen die Kolonnen den Grumeti-Fluss — die erste große Überquerung des Jahres, weniger berühmt als die am Mara, aber dennoch spektakulär, mit gewaltigen Krokodilen, die in den Untiefen warten.

Juli bis Oktober ist aus gutem Grund Hochsaison. Die Herden drängen in die nördliche Serengeti und beginnen den Mara-Fluss zu überqueren, oft mehrfach hin und her. Überquerungen sind unberechenbar: Man kann einen ganzen Tag vergeblich warten oder innerhalb von Minuten nach der Ankunft zwanzigtausend Gnus ins Wasser stürzen sehen. Wir planen für Gäste, die diesen Moment erleben wollen, stets mindestens drei Nächte im Norden ein.

Im November ziehen die kurzen Regenfälle die Herden wieder südwärts. Im Dezember verteilen sie sich über die östliche Serengeti und kehren auf die Kalbungsgründe zurück — und der Kreislauf beginnt von Neuem. Unser Rat: Wählen Sie eine Phase, die Sie begeistert, und bauen Sie die Reise darum herum. Es gibt keinen schlechten Monat — nur unterschiedliche Belohnungen.

posts.title: Hinter der Linse: Tarangires große Stoßzahn-Elefanten
posts.excerpt: Die Giganten fotografieren — und warum Tarangires Elefanten einzigartig sind.
body: Tarangire beherbergt eine der größten Elefantenkonzentrationen Ostafrikas und — entscheidend — eine der letzten Hochburgen wahrer Stoßzahnträger: Bullen, deren Elfenbein bis zum Boden reicht. Jahrzehnte sorgfältigen Schutzes haben es ermöglicht, dass diese Genetik hier überlebt hat, während sie anderswo weitgehend verschwunden ist.

Die Trockenzeit von Juli bis Oktober ist die magische Phase. Wenn die umliegenden Gebiete austrocknen, strömen die Herden zum Tarangire-Fluss. Wir haben dreihundert Elefanten in einer einzigen Flusskrümmung gezählt — trinkend und staubbadend im goldenen Nachmittagslicht.

Für die Fotografie empfiehlt sich eine niedrige Position. Bringen Sie Ihr Objektiv nah an den Boden und fotografieren Sie gegen das Licht in der letzten Stunde vor Sonnenuntergang — der aufgewirbelte Staub der Herde wird zum leuchtenden Heiligenschein. Ein 100–400-mm-Zoom ist ideal: lang genug für Porträts, weit genug für Familiengruppen.

Beobachten Sie das Verhalten: Matriarchinnen, die die Herde im Gänsemarsch zum Wasser führen; Bullen, die halbherzig in den Untiefen sparren; winzige Kälber, die zwischen den Beinen der Erwachsenen hindurchrennen. Seien Sie geduldig und leise — Tarangires Elefanten sind entspannt gegenüber Fahrzeugen, aber Stille belohnen sie mit außergewöhnlicher Nähe.

posts.title: Der Erstbesucher-Leitfaden für Tansania
posts.excerpt: Visa, Impfungen, Packliste — alles, was Sie vor Ihrer ersten Safari wissen müssen.
body: Eine Safari in Tansania zu planen kann zunächst überwältigend wirken, aber die Grundlagen sind unkompliziert. Die meisten Nationalitäten können vor der Reise ein E-Visum online beantragen oder ein Visum bei Ankunft am Kilimanjaro oder Dar es Salaam erhalten. Eine Gelbfieberimpfung ist nur erforderlich, wenn Sie aus einem Land mit Übertragungsrisiko einreisen; wir empfehlen stets, sechs bis acht Wochen vor Abreise eine Reiseklinik aufzusuchen.

Malariaprophylaxe ist Standard — die meisten Gäste verwenden Malarone oder Doxycyclin. Packen Sie langärmelige Hemden und Hosen in gedeckten Farben ein (vermeiden Sie Blau und Schwarz, die in manchen Gebieten Tsetsefliegen anziehen). Schichten sind entscheidend: Morgens am Kraterrand kann es nahe dem Gefrierpunkt sein, während nachmittags in der Ebene über 30 °C herrschen.

Gepäckgrenzen bei Buschflügen liegen typischerweise bei 15 kg in Weichtaschen. Wir stellen nach der Buchung eine Packliste zur Verfügung. Die Kurzfassung: zwei Hosen, drei Hemden, ein Fleece, eine Windjacke, feste Wanderschuhe, Sandalen, Sonnenhut, Sonnenbrille, Sonnencreme und ein kleiner Tagesrucksack. Kamera, Fernglas und eine Stirnlampe runden die Ausrüstung ab.

Trinkgeld ist üblich und von großer Bedeutung — Guides, Camp-Personal und Träger sind darauf angewiesen. Wir liefern eine klare Trinkgeldrichtlinie, damit es keine Überraschungen gibt. Tansanische Schilling sind für kleine Einkäufe nützlich, aber US-Dollar (saubere Scheine ab 2009) werden fast überall akzeptiert.
Vor allem: Lassen Sie in Ihrem Reiseplan Raum, um nichts zu tun. Die besten Safari-Momente stehen in keinem Programm.

posts.title: Kilimandscharo besteigen: Routen im Vergleich
posts.excerpt: Marangu, Machame, Lemosho, Northern Circuit — den richtigen Weg zum Uhuru Peak finden.
body: Der Kilimandscharo hat sieben etablierte Routen, doch vier sind für nahezu alle erfolgreichen Gipfelbesteigungen verantwortlich. Die richtige Wahl ist der wichtigste Faktor dafür, ob Sie am Uhuru Peak stehen — weit wichtiger als Fitness oder Ausrüstung.

Die Marangu-Route (5–6 Tage) ist die klassische ‚Coca-Cola-Route' mit Hüttenunterkünften. Sie ist die günstigste und die einzige Route mit Betten, aber der kurze Zeitplan lässt wenig Raum zur Akklimatisierung — die Gipfelerfolgsrate liegt bei etwa 50 %. Wir empfehlen sie selten.

Die Machame-Route (6–7 Tage) ist landschaftlich reizvoller, anspruchsvoller und weitaus beliebter. Die Route folgt dem Prinzip ‚Hoch steigen, tief schlafen', was die Akklimatisierung fördert. Die Erfolgsrate steigt bei der 7-Tage-Variante auf 75–85 %. Dies ist unsere Standardempfehlung für fitte Trekker mit knappem Zeitplan.

Die Lemosho-Route (7–8 Tage) führt von Westen heran und gilt als die schönste Route. Ruhiger als Machame, mit hervorragender Akklimatisierung und Gipfelerfolgsraten über 90 % bei der 8-Tage-Variante. Wenn Sie die Zeit haben, ist dies die richtige Wahl.

Der Northern Circuit (9 Tage) ist die längste und neueste Route. Er umrundet die Nordhänge, die nur wenige Trekker je zu Gesicht bekommen. Die Gipfelerfolgsrate übersteigt 95 %. Er ist unsere Empfehlung für Gäste, die die höchsten Chancen auf dem Dach Afrikas wünschen und die Einsamkeit schätzen.
Welche Route Sie auch wählen: Trainieren Sie mindestens drei Monate mit Wanderungen unter Gewicht, nehmen Sie sich Zeit und hören Sie auf Ihre Guides. Der Berg ist geduldig — seien Sie es auch.

posts.title: Ballonfahrt über die Serengeti im Morgengrauen
posts.excerpt: Lautlos über die Ebenen schweben, während die Sonne aufgeht — eine Perspektive, die nur wenige kennen.
body: Wir stehen vor Sonnenaufgang im Korb, die Brenner zischen über uns, die Ebenen sind noch violett im Halbdunkel. Innerhalb von Minuten sinkt die Serengeti unter uns hinweg, und die Welt wird still — nur der Wind ist zu hören.

Aus tausend Fuß Höhe sieht die Migration aus wie ein sich langsam bewegender Fluss. Man erkennt die Struktur der Landschaft — die Kopjes, die Flusskrümmungen, die Waldinseln — in einer Weise, wie es keine Pirschfahrt zeigen kann. Löwen auf einer Beute, Elefanten in Familienverbänden, Giraffen, die in den Baumkronen fressen: alles gleichzeitig sichtbar, in einem einzigen Bild.

Der Flug dauert etwa eine Stunde. Die Landung ist sanft, meist in der offenen Ebene, wo ein Champagner-Frühstück unter einem Akazienbaum aufgebaut ist. Es ist ein Luxus — aber für Flitterwöchner, Fotografen und alle, die einen besonderen Anlass feiern, ist es die Art von Erinnerung, die eine ganze Reise verankert.
Buchen Sie frühzeitig. In der zentralen Serengeti sind nur eine Handvoll Ballons im Einsatz, und die Hochsaison ist Monate im Voraus ausgebucht.

posts.title: Kulturelle Begegnungen mit den Maasai
posts.excerpt: Wie wir mit lokalen Gemeinschaften für authentische, respektvolle Erlebnisse zusammenarbeiten.
body: Der ‚Kulturbesuch' hat zu Recht einen schlechten Ruf erworben. Zu viele Veranstalter betreiben ein rein transaktionales Modell: Touristen kommen an, Fotos werden gemacht, eine Gebühr wird bezahlt, alle gehen nach Hause. Die Gemeinschaft dient nur als Kulisse. Wir haben Jahre damit verbracht, etwas Anderes aufzubauen.

Unsere Partnergemeinschaften liegen an den Grenzen des Ngorongoro-Schutzgebiets und rund um Loliondo. Besuche werden über gemeindegeführte Stiftungen organisiert, nicht über Mittelsmänner. Die Gebühr pro Besucher fließt direkt in Schulen, Wasserprojekte und Frauenkooperativen, und die Gemeinschaft entscheidet, was geteilt wird und was nicht.

Was Gäste tatsächlich erleben, variiert je nach Gemeinschaft. Sie könnten mit einem Maasai-Ältesten wandern und lernen, den Busch zu lesen, mit Frauen beim Perlenhandwerk sitzen oder an einem Viehsegen teilnehmen. Es gibt keine inszenierten Tänze — nur das, was an diesem Tag tatsächlich stattfindet.

Fotografieregeln: Fragen Sie jedes Mal zuerst. Ein aufrichtiges Lächeln und ein Moment des Gesprächs bringen Sie weiter als jedes Trinkgeld. Viele Älteste bitten darum, nicht fotografiert zu werden — dieser Wunsch ist nicht verhandelbar.

Die Maasai sind kein Museum. Sie sind eine lebendige, sich entwickelnde Gesellschaft mit Mobiltelefonen, Universitätsstudenten und Fußballvereinen. Das Privileg eines Besuchs ist die Chance, ihnen so zu begegnen, wie sie wirklich sind.

posts.title: Leoparden-Spurensuche in Seronera
posts.excerpt: Warum die Granitkopjes der zentralen Serengeti Afrikas Leopardenhauptstadt sind.
body: Die Seronera-Ebene in der zentralen Serengeti weist die höchste Leopardendichte ganz Afrikas auf. Der Grund liegt in der Geografie: Ein Netz aus ganzjährig wasserführenden Flüssen, gesäumt von Leberwurstbäumen und Feigenbäumen, bietet Schatten, Deckung für den Hinterhalt und erhöhte Tagesverstecke. Wenn Sie einen Leoparden sehen möchten, sind Sie hier richtig.

Wir starten vor Morgengrauen. Leoparden sind in der Morgenkühle und wieder im letzten Abendlicht am aktivsten. Unsere Guides kennen die einzelnen Tiere beim Namen — das Weibchen mit dem Knick im Schwanz, den großen Revierbullen mit der gekerbten Ohrmuschel — und wir fahren die Flusskorridore langsam ab, jeden waagerechten Ast musternd.

Achten Sie auf Alarmrufe von Impalas, das Geschnatter der Grünen Meerkatzen und kreisende Geier. Eine in einen Baum geschleppte Beute kann einen Leoparden zwei Tage lang an einem Ort halten. Sobald wir einen gefunden haben, warten wir. Ein schlafender Leopard wird sich irgendwann strecken, gähnen und herabsteigen — und dieser ruhige Moment der Bewegung ist das Foto der Reise.
Etikette ist wichtig: Abstand halten, Motor aus, das Tier nicht bedrängen. Andere Fahrzeuge werden kommen, aber ein umsichtiger Guide findet in der Regel einen ruhigeren Blickwinkel.

posts.title: In unserem Northern Camp
posts.excerpt: Zeltluxus richtig gemacht — ein stiller Abend, während die Herden vorbeiziehen.
body: Unser saisonales Camp in der nördlichen Serengeti liegt auf einem flachen Höhenrücken über dem Mara-Fluss. Es ist ein kleiner Betrieb — acht Zelte, kein Elektrozaun, kein Swimmingpool. Was es bietet, ist Stille, ungehinderter Blick auf die Überquerungsstellen und ein Team, das jeden Gast innerhalb einer Stunde nach Ankunft beim Namen kennt.

Jedes Zelt steht auf einer erhöhten Hartholzplattform: Kingsize-Bett, eigenes Bad mit Dusche, ein Schreibtisch und eine private Veranda. Solarstrom versorgt die Beleuchtung; heißes Wasser kommt aus einem holzbefeuerten Boiler, der zweimal täglich beheizt wird. Der Gedanke ist Komfort ohne Abschottung von der Umgebung.

Der Abend beginnt mit einem Sundowner auf dem Höhenrücken — Gin, Tonic, ein Tablett Biltong und die Sonne, die hinter der Steilstufe versinkt. Das Dinner besteht aus drei Gängen an einem langen Gemeinschaftstisch, danach Kaffee am Feuer, während ein Guide die Sichtungen des Tages bespricht.

Wir verlegen das Camp jede Saison, um den Herden zu folgen. Wenn Sie im August oder September kommen, könnte Ihr Zelt einen Kilometer von einer Flussüberquerung entfernt stehen. Diese Nähe ist durch nichts zu ersetzen.

posts.title: Was man auf Safari isst
posts.excerpt: Buschfrühstück, Sundowner und die überraschende Raffinesse der Camp-Küche.
body: Die Camp-Küche in Tansania hat sich weit von Doseneintopf-Klischees entfernt. Die meisten unserer Partnercamps beschäftigen ausgebildete Köche, bauen eigene Kräuter an und lassen täglich frische Produkte einfliegen. Erwarten Sie drei vollwertige Mahlzeiten am Tag, plus ein heißes Getränk, das zum Aufwachen an Ihr Zelt gebracht wird.

Frühstück im Busch ist eine Tradition, die man mindestens einmal erleben sollte: ein Klapptisch, weißes Leinen, frisches Obst, heiße Eier und Speck — alles unter einer Akazie aufgebaut nach der frühen Pirschfahrt. Kaffee hat nie besser geschmeckt.

Das Mittagessen ist üblicherweise ein leichtes Buffet im Camp — Salate, kalter Aufschnitt, ein warmes Gericht, frisches Brot. Viele Gäste ziehen sich zu einer Siesta zurück, bis die Nachmittagsfahrt beginnt.
Sundowner sind heilig. Eine Flasche Gin, ein Beutel Oliven, die Sonne, die über den Ebenen untergeht. Dann folgt das Dinner: drei Gänge, oft bei Kerzenschein, fast immer unter dem Sternenhimmel.

Besondere Ernährungswünsche werden problemlos berücksichtigt — vegetarisch, vegan, glutenfrei, koscher und halal können bei rechtzeitiger Mitteilung alle umgesetzt werden. Teilen Sie es uns bei der Buchung mit, und die Küche erledigt den Rest.

faq.ctaDesc: Still have questions? Our specialists are happy to help.

items.q: When is the best time to see the Great Migration?
items.a: The migration is an annual cycle, so there is always action in the Serengeti. January–February is calving season in the south near Ndutu. June–July the herds move through the western Serengeti and cross the Grumeti River. July–October is when the famous Mara River crossings happen in the north. November–December sees the herds return south. We tailor your itinerary to whichever phase interests you most.

items.q: How far in advance do I need to book gorilla permits?
items.a: Gorilla trekking permits for Bwindi Impenetrable Forest (Uganda) are limited and in high demand. We recommend booking at least 3–6 months in advance, and up to a year ahead for peak months (June–September). Contact us early and we will handle permit allocation on your behalf.

items.q: Do I need a visa for Tanzania / Uganda?
items.a: Most nationalities including US and UK citizens require a visa for Tanzania, Uganda, and Rwanda. Tanzania offers an e-visa online before travel. Uganda visas can be obtained on arrival or online. We provide detailed, up-to-date visa guidance tailored to your nationality upon booking — requirements change, so always verify with the relevant embassy.

items.q: What vaccinations and health precautions do I need?
items.a: Malaria prophylaxis is strongly recommended for Tanzania and Uganda — consult your doctor or a travel health clinic. Yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from a yellow fever country and is recommended for Uganda. Other common recommendations include hepatitis A, typhoid, and tetanus. Always consult a qualified travel health professional at least 6–8 weeks before departure.

items.q: What is included in the safari price?
items.a: Our safari prices include a 4WD vehicle with pop-up roof, experienced English-speaking driver-guide, all accommodation and meals per the itinerary, national park entrance fees, mineral water on game drives, government taxes, and Flying Doctor Society emergency evacuation membership. International flights, visas, travel insurance, tips, and personal items are not included.

items.q: What currencies and payment methods do you accept?
items.a: We accept payment in USD, EUR, and GBP. Bank wire transfer is our primary payment method for deposits and balances. Please contact us and we will confirm current payment options including whether card payment is available.

Cancellations 90+ days before departure incur a USD 500 per person fee. 89–60 days: 20% of total tour rate. 59–30 days: 50%. 29 days or fewer: 100% forfeiture. We strongly recommend trip cancellation insurance. In some cases we can hold your deposit as a credit note for a future trip.

items.q: Is Tanzania / Uganda safe for travellers?
items.a: Tanzania is one of Africa's most stable and safe tourism destinations. Our vehicles are equipped with radios and first aid kits, our guides are trained in visitor management, and all guests are enrolled in the Flying Doctor Society for emergency evacuation. We monitor conditions continuously and communicate any relevant updates before and during your trip.

items.q: Are your safaris suitable for families with children?
items.a: Yes — we design family safaris regularly. We recommend children be at least 6 years old for game drives. Gorilla trekking requires participants to be at least 15 years old. Kilimanjaro climbs are typically suitable for fit teenagers aged 14+. Tell us the ages of your children and we will tailor an appropriate itinerary.

items.q: Can solo travellers join a group safari?
items.a: Absolutely. We operate both group departures and private, customised itineraries for solo travellers. A single supplement applies for solo room occupancy on some tours. Contact us and we will advise on the best option — including whether joining an existing group departure makes sense for your dates.

items.q: What should I pack for a safari?
items.a: Lightweight neutral-coloured clothing (khaki, olive, tan — avoid white and bright colours); a good sun hat; sunscreen; insect repellent; comfortable walking shoes or boots; a light fleece or jacket for early mornings; binoculars; and a camera with a telephoto lens if possible. serengeti-northern-migration.title: Serengeti Northern Migration
serengeti-northern-migration.intro: The northern part of Tanzania is renowned for its stunning landscapes and rich wildlife experiences. This region encompasses several world-famous parks and conservation areas. Here are some luxurious sample itineraries focused on the northern circuit, combining iconic destinations with high-end accommodations and exclusive experiences.

days.title: DAY 1:Karibu! Safari begins!
days.body: A representative from Aardvark Safaris Tanzania will meet and greet you as soon as you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport and take you to the Mt. Meru Hotel, for your overnight. Arusha, nestled in the shadow of majestic Mount Meru, is a dynamic, fast- growing town and a famed embarkation point for Tanzania safaris. Because of its altitude (roughly 4,600 feet above sea level), Arusha is blessed with a pleasant climate, perfect for the coffee plantations that surround it.

days.title: DAY 2 &3: Tarangire National Park
days.body: Staying two nights at the amazing Kichuguu Camp, built in 2017 and rated Excel- lent on TripAdvisor. You’ll love the service, the food, the surrounding wildness, the eco- friendly design. Here we will have the rare opportunity to do a night game drive, a privi- lege that few safari goers can get today. We’ll look for nocturnal mammals that few see (for example, civet, genet, African porcupine, maybe even the odd aardvark) and preda- tors during their most-active periods. Lions and leopards at night are completely differ- ent from the snoozing animals to be found in mid-day. We feel that a night drive could well be among the finest highlights of your entire safari. Kichuguu Camp

days.title: DAY 4: Driving to Lake Manyara.
days.body: This small but productive park includes the western wall of the Great Rift Valley and lies at 3,150-feet altitude. It is noted for its high elephant population and tree-climbing lions. Flamingos, pelicans, storks, and hippos inhabit the lakeshore; which is surrounded by groundwater forest, with fig, palm, tama- rind, and baobab trees hosting blue and vervet monkeys, baboons, hornbills, and much more. We may encounter bushbucks, waterbucks, giraffes (some surprisingly dark), im- pala, perhaps even a monitor lizard. Over- night: Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge

days.title: DAY 5: Ngorongoro Crater.
days.body: Brace yourself for a trip back into the Pleistocene! Today we’ll explore one of the world’s largest calderas, 10-11 miles in diameter and 2500 feet deep. This diverse ecosystem of forests, swamps, grasslands, and lakes supports lion, cheetah, serval, hyena, three kinds of jackal, zebra, rhino, hippo, elephant, and thousands of antelopes, including the massive eland. Because poaching is not a problem here, rare black rhinos and elephants with enormous tusks are present. It’s also a birding hotspot. Walt has recorded over 100 species of birds in a day even when most of our time has been watching big mammals! Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge.

days.title: DAY 6 - 10 : Serengeti National Park.
days.body: Five full days in the fabled Serengeti, one of the most productive and important wildlife areas in the world. With its vast rolling plains, dramatic outcrops of Precambrian rocks (kopjes), flat-topped acacias, crocodile- and hippo-inhabited rivers lined with riverine gallery forests, and huge herds of animals, the Serengeti is about the ultimate in “wild Africa.” The famous “Great Migration” of wildebeest, zebra, and oth- er grazing herbivores is one of the last mass movements of animals still taking place on earth. We could not be here at a better time of year! There is a lot of history here—both human and animal—and you will be enriched and informed by our guides. We’ll spend our first night at Pamoja Tented Lodge (or equivalent) in the central Serengeti, which is noted for leopards, hippo pools, and the Maasai Kopjes. Then we’ll proceed north for three nights at Mara Mara Kati Kati Tented Camp, which should be close to the heart of the migration, and we will venture to some areas of extraordinary beauty where large predators thrive. With good luck, we hope to see the herds undertaking the treacherous crossing of the Mara River. Camping in the Serengeti surrounded by the exotic sounds of wild Africa is truly an in-tents experience!

days.title: DAY 11: Serengeti, Oldupai Gorge, Crater Highlands.
days.body: After our final breakfast in the Serengeti, we’ll drive across the plains, ascending again into the high- lands of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a World Heritage Site dedicated to the peaceful union of pastoralism, conservation of natural resources, and responsible tourism. We will stop to visit Oldupai (or Olduvai) Gorge, world-renowned for the discoveries of early hominids made by archaeologists Mary and Louis Leakey. We will visit the wonderful museum here and, if time permits, explore the gorge where the discoveries were made.

days.title: DAY 12: Arusha.
days.body: Today we drive back to Arusha for a visit to the Cultural Heritage Center (wonderful wildlife art gallery and excellent shopping, including for precious Tanzanite jewelry), a scrumptious buffet lunch, and some time to rest and prepare for your trip home that evening or for continuation to Mkomazi National Park for those doing the extension. Day rooms or overnight at Mt. Meru Hotel., depending on your plans.

We will walk to the rim of the Ngurdoto Crater, more accurately a caldera or vol- canic collapse feature. We will scan the caldera floor for wildlife and watch the skies for birds of prey or other aerial masters. From the rim forest, we will proceed through wood- lands and past lakes and marshes, watching for giraffes, waterbucks, kingfishers, and much more. On former lava (volcanic mudflow) deposits are the Momela Lakes, alkaline havens for multitudes of waterbirds, including flamingos, ducks and geese, shorebirds, storks, and ibises. Many visitors to Tanzania head directly to the savannah parks and miss the lush, green beauty and special wildlife of this park, a naturalist’s favorite. Most of the Datoga today are farmers specializing in onion plantations, and some are superb metal smiths who make the arrows for the Hadza. Lake Ndutu offers excellent birdwatching. Camping will provide an immersive experience in the Serengeti’s natural beauty.

days.title: DAY 8: Serengeti, Oldupai Gorge, Crater Highlands.
days.body: After our final breakfast in the Serengeti, we’ll drive east across the plains, ascending again into the highlands of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a World Heritage Site dedicated to the peaceful union of pastoralism, conservation of natural resources, and responsible tourism. We will stop to visit Oldupai (or Olduvai) Gorge, world-renowned for the discoveries of early hominids made by archaeologists Mary and Louis Leakey. We will visit the small museum here and explore the gorge where the discoveries were made. For many people, a visit to Oldupai is a pilgrimage to one of the world’s greatest archeo- logical sites, a place where we can vicariously connect with our distant ancestors. We may also visit a Maasai Village. Thereafter, we will drive out of the park to relax at the Ngoron- goro Farm House, whose lovely gardens provide scrumptious produce for this oasis and for some of the remote tented camps. Tonight we will share highlights of the safari as we prepare tomorrow to depart from Arusha.

days.title: DAY 9: Arusha.
days.body: Today we return to Arusha for visit to the Cultural Heritage Center. lunch, and an optional visit to the St Lucia Hospice and Orphanage for victims of HIV/AIDS that was founded by Augustine’s heroic wife, Winfrida. Day rooms at Mount Meru Hotel. Evening transfer to the airport for those fly- ing out of country and the beginning of hours of reflection on our amazing experiences. Those extending to Uganda will have another night at the Mt. Meru Hotel.

days.title: DAY 10: Arusha, Tanzania.
days.body: As the Tanzania safari closes, the Uganda one begins. Continuing participants will enjoy our fine dinner at Mt. Meru Hotel anticipating the adventure ahead in the land of Mountain Gorillas, Chimpanzees, and spectacular birds and mammals. . . . Kampala, Uganda. Folks doing only the Uganda trip will arrive at Entebbe Airport and transfer to the Lake Victoria Serena Resort for overnight and breakfast.

exploring-cape-town-victoria-falls-botsw.title: Cape Town, Victoria Falls & Botswana Wildlife Circuit
exploring-cape-town-victoria-falls-botsw.intro: A southern Africa circuit from Cape Town through Victoria Falls into Botswana's premier wildlife areas — Chobe, Hwange, and the Okavango Delta — combining city, waterfall, and bush in one journey.
exploring-cape-town-victoria-falls-botsw.route: Victoria Falls · Chobe · Hwange · Okavango Delta

days.title: DAY 1:Karibu! Safari begins!
days.body: A representative from Aardvark Safaris Tanzania will meet and greet you as soon as you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport and take you to the Mt. Meru Hotel, for your overnight. Arusha, nestled in the shadow of majestic Mount Meru, is a dynamic, fast- growing town and a famed embarkation point for Tanzania safaris. Because of its altitude (roughly 4,600 feet above sea level), Arusha is blessed with a pleasant climate, perfect for the coffee plantations that surround it.

days.title: DAY 2 &3: Tarangire National Park
days.body: Staying two nights at the amazing Kichuguu Camp, built in 2017 and rated Excel- lent on TripAdvisor. You’ll love the service, the food, the surrounding wildness, the eco- friendly design. Here we will have the rare opportunity to do a night game drive, a privi- lege that few safari goers can get today. We’ll look for nocturnal mammals that few see (for example, civet, genet, African porcupine, maybe even the odd aardvark) and preda- tors during their most-active periods. Lions and leopards at night are completely differ- ent from the snoozing animals to be found in mid-day. We feel that a night drive could well be among the finest highlights of your entire safari. Kichuguu Camp

days.title: DAY 4: Driving to Lake Manyara.
days.body: This small but productive park includes the western wall of the Great Rift Valley and lies at 3,150-feet altitude. It is noted for its high elephant population and tree-climbing lions. Flamingos, pelicans, storks, and hippos inhabit the lakeshore; which is surrounded by groundwater forest, with fig, palm, tama- rind, and baobab trees hosting blue and vervet monkeys, baboons, hornbills, and much more. We may encounter bushbucks, waterbucks, giraffes (some surprisingly dark), im- pala, perhaps even a monitor lizard. Over- night: Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge

days.title: DAY 5: Ngorongoro Crater.
days.body: Brace yourself for a trip back into the Pleistocene! Today we’ll explore one of the world’s largest calderas, 10-11 miles in diameter and 2500 feet deep. This diverse ecosystem of forests, swamps, grasslands, and lakes supports lion, cheetah, serval, hyena, three kinds of jackal, zebra, rhino, hippo, elephant, and thousands of antelopes, including the massive eland. Because poaching is not a problem here, rare black rhinos and elephants with enormous tusks are present. It’s also a birding hotspot. Walt has recorded over 100 species of birds in a day even when most of our time has been watching big mammals! Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge.

days.title: DAY 6 - 10 : Serengeti National Park.
days.body: Five full days in the fabled Serengeti, one of the most productive and important wildlife areas in the world. With its vast rolling plains, dramatic outcrops of Precambrian rocks (kopjes), flat-topped acacias, crocodile- and hippo-inhabited rivers lined with riverine gallery forests, and huge herds of animals, the Serengeti is about the ultimate in “wild Africa.” The famous “Great Migration” of wildebeest, zebra, and oth- er grazing herbivores is one of the last mass movements of animals still taking place on earth. We could not be here at a better time of year! There is a lot of history here—both human and animal—and you will be enriched and informed by our guides. We’ll spend our first night at Pamoja Tented Lodge (or equivalent) in the central Serengeti, which is noted for leopards, hippo pools, and the Maasai Kopjes. Then we’ll proceed north for three nights at Mara Mara Kati Kati Tented Camp, which should be close to the heart of the migration, and we will venture to some areas of extraordinary beauty where large predators thrive. With good luck, we hope to see the herds undertaking the treacherous crossing of the Mara River. Camping in the Serengeti surrounded by the exotic sounds of wild Africa is truly an in-tents experience!

days.title: DAY 11: Serengeti, Oldupai Gorge, Crater Highlands.
days.body: After our final breakfast in the Serengeti, we’ll drive across the plains, ascending again into the high- lands of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a World Heritage Site dedicated to the peaceful union of pastoralism, conservation of natural resources, and responsible tourism. We will stop to visit Oldupai (or Olduvai) Gorge, world-renowned for the discoveries of early hominids made by archaeologists Mary and Louis Leakey. We will visit the wonderful museum here and, if time permits, explore the gorge where the discoveries were made.

days.title: DAY 12: Arusha.
days.body: Today we drive back to Arusha for a visit to the Cultural Heritage Center (wonderful wildlife art gallery and excellent shopping, including for precious Tanzanite jewelry), a scrumptious buffet lunch, and some time to rest and prepare for your trip home that evening or for continuation to Mkomazi National Park for those doing the extension. Day rooms or overnight at Mt. Meru Hotel., depending on your plans.

northern-circuit-route.title: Northern Circuit Route
northern-circuit-route.intro: Mount Kilimanjaro is an iconic landmark in Tanzania and Africa’s highest mountain, rising approximately 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) above sea level. It’s known as a “freestanding” mountain due to its isolated prominence, unlike most mountains, which are part of larger ranges. Here’s an overview of the mountain and what makes it unique:
northern-circuit-route.route: Mti Mkubwa · Shira · Moir · Buffalo · School Hut · Uhuru Peak

days.title: DAY 1: Arrive Kilimanjaro Airport (JRO) Tanzania.
days.body: Elevation: 9,498 ft Hiking Time: 3-4 hoursDistance: 7 km | 4 miles Habitat: Rain Forest. Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO), you will be met outside customs area by a driver guide holding a sign board written clearly your booking name and drive to Arusha for overnight at ARUSHA SERENA LODGE.

days.title: DAY 2: Mti Mkubwa (Big tree Camp)
days.body: Elevation: 9,498 ft Hiking Time: 3-4 hours Distance: 7 km | 4 miles Habitat: Rain Forest. We depart Moshi for Londorossi Gate, which takes about 4 hours, where you will complete entry formalities. Then drive to the Lemosho trailhead. Upon arrival at trailhead, we begin hiking through undisturbed forest which winds to the first camp site. Dinner and overnight at MTI MKUBWA (BIGTREE CAMP).

days.title: DAY 3: Shira 1 Camp
days.body: Elevation: 11,500 ft Hiking Time: 5-6 hours Distance: 8 km | 5 miles Habitat: Heather or moorland. We continue on the trail leading out of the rain forest and into a savannah of tall grasses, heather and volcanic rock draped with lichen beards. As we ascend through the lush rolling hills and cross several streams, we reach the Shira Ridge before dropping gently down to Shira 1 Camp. Here we catch our first glimpse of Kibo across the plateau. Dinner and overnight at SHIRA 1 Camp

days.title: DAY 4: Shira 2 Camp
days.body: Elevation: 12,500 ft Hiking Time: 3-4 hours Distance: 10 km | 4 miles Habitat: HeatherWe explore the Shira Plateau. It is a gentle walk east on moorland meadows towards Shira 2 Camp. The heath zone displays abundant wildflowers and unique Senecio trees. Dinner and overnight at SHIRA 2 CAMP.

days.title: DAY 5 : Moir Hut
days.body: Elevation: 13,580 ft Hiking Time: 7 hours Distance: 7 km | 4 miles Habitat: Alpine Desert We continue to the east up a ridge and then head southeast to Lava Tower for lunch – a 300ft tall volcanic rock formation at the elevation of 15,190ft. Then we divert from the main trail to Moir Hut, a little used site on the base of Lent Hills. A variety of walks are available on Lent Hills making this an excellent acclimatization opportunity. Shira Plateau is one of the highest plateaus on earth. Dinner and overnight at MOIR HUT

days.title: DAY 6: Buffalo Camp
days.body: Elevation: 13,200 ft Hiking Time: 5-7 hours Distance: 12 km | 7 miles Habitat: Alpine DesertWe trek out of Moir Valley with a moderately steep climb, then hike to the summit of Lent Hills before returning to the main trail. The path crosses a rock field and gently undulates before reaching Buffalo Camp. This section of the trail offers great views across the plains that lie north of Kilimanjaro and stretch out to the Kenyan/Tanzanian border. Dinner and overnight at BUFALO CAMP.

days.title: DAY 7: Third Cave
days.body: Elevation: 12,700 ft Hiking Time: 5-7 hoursDistance: 8 km | 5 milesHabitat: Heather As we head up Buffalo Ridge, the terrain becomes increasingly sparse. This route is rarely travelled and we will enjoy its mountain wilderness feel. We trek through remote valleys on to the northern slopes of Kilimanjaro until we arrive at Third Cave. Dinner and Overnight at THIRD CAVE.

days.title: DAY 8: School Hut
days.body: Elevation: 15,600 ft Hiking Time: 4-5 hours Distance: 5 km | 3 miles Habitat: Alpine Desert We climb steadily up and over the “Saddle,” which sits between Kibo and Mawenzi. We continue on to our camp, School Hut. Once here we rest, enjoy an early dinner to prepare for the summit day.

days.title: DAY 9: Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
days.body: Elevation: 19,341 ft to 10,065 ft Hiking Time: 13 hours Habitat: Arctic to Rain forest Very early in the morning (around midnight), we begin our push to the summit. This is the most mentally and physically challenging portion of the trek. The wind and cold at this elevation and time of day can be extreme. We ascend in the darkness for several hours while taking frequent, but short, breaks. At Gilman’s point (18,600 ft), you will be rewarded with the most magnificent sunrise you are ever likely to see coming over Mawenzi Peak. Finally, we arrive at Uhuru Peak- the highest point on Mount Kilimanjaro and the continent of Africa. From the summit, we now make our descent continuing straight down to the Mweka Hut camp site, stopping at Barafu for lunch. The trail is very rocky and can be quite hard on the knees; trekking poles are helpful. Mweka Camp is situated in the upper forest and mist or rain can be expected in the late afternoon. Later in the evening, we enjoy our last dinner on the mountain and a well-earned sleep.

days.title: DAY 10: Mweka Gate
days.body: Elevation: 5,380 ft Hiking Time: 3-4 hours Distance: 10 km | 6 miles Habitat: Rain Forest. On our last day, we continue the descent to Mweka Gate and collect the summit certificates. At lower elevations, it can be wet and muddy. From the gate, we continue another hour to Mweka Village. A vehicle will meet us at Mweka Village to drive us back to the hotel in Arusha and overnight at ARUSHA SERENA LODGE.

iconic-tanzania.title: Iconic Tanzania: Quick Escape to Tarangire, Ngorongoro & Serengeti
iconic-tanzania.intro: The northern part of Tanzania is renowned for its stunning landscapes and rich wildlife experiences. This region encompasses several world-famous parks and conservation areas. Here are some luxurious sample itineraries focused on the northern circuit, combining iconic destinations with high-end accommodations and exclusive experiences.

days.title: Day 1: Arrival & Tarangire National Park
days.body: Morning: Depart from Arusha and drive to Tarangire National Park, known for its iconic baobab trees and large elephant herds. Afternoon: Enjoy a game drive, spotting diverse wildlife like zebras, wildebeest, and lions near the Tarangire River. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or camp near Tarangire.

days.title: Day 2: Ngorongoro Crater Exploration
days.body: Morning: Head to Ngorongoro Conservation Area and descend into the world-famous Ngorongoro Crater. Afternoon: Explore the lush crater floor on a game drive, where you may see the Big Five—lions, elephants, rhinos, buffalo, and leopards. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or camp on the rim of the crater.

days.title: Day 3: Serengeti National Park (Central)
days.body: Morning: Drive from Ngorongoro to the Serengeti, passing through the highlands with scenic views of the savannah. Afternoon: Enjoy a game drive in the central Serengeti, observing vast herds, predators, and diverse birdlife. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or tented camp in the central Serengeti.

days.title: Day 4: Serengeti & Return to Arusha
days.body: Morning: Early morning game drive in the Serengeti, capturing the sunrise and spotting active predators. Midday: Start the journey back to Arusha, with an optional flight for those seeking a faster return. Evening: Arrive in Arusha for onward travel or departure.

crater-savannah.title: Crater Savannah
crater-savannah.intro: A focused northern Tanzania escape pairing Tarangire's baobab woodlands with the wildlife-rich floor of Ngorongoro Crater — ideal when time is short but you want iconic game viewing.

days.title: Day 1: Arrival & Tarangire National Park
days.body: Morning: Depart from Arusha and drive to Tarangire National Park, renowned for its ancient baobab trees and large elephant herds. Afternoon: Enjoy a game drive along the Tarangire River, spotting wildlife such as zebras, wildebeest, lions, and various bird species. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or camp near Tarangire.

days.title: Day 2: Tarangire National Park & ​​Transfer to Ngorongoro
days.body: Morning: Start the day with a game drive in Tarangire, capturing more of the park’s unique wildlife and scenic landscapes. Afternoon: Depart for the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, enjoying scenic views along the way. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or camp on the rim of Ngorongoro Crater, preparing for an early descent into the crater the following day.

quick-escape.title: Quick Escape
quick-escape.intro: A compact overnight circuit to the Ngorongoro Crater rim and floor — maximum wildlife in minimum time, with scenic highland drives and the Big Five on the crater floor.

days.title: Day 1: Arrival & Transfer to Ngorongoro Conservation Area
days.body: Morning: Depart from Arusha and enjoy a scenic drive to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Afternoon: Arrive at the Ngorongoro Crater rim, where you’ll have time to take in the breathtaking views from above and perhaps enjoy a short nature walk in the surrounding area. Evening: Overnight at a lodge or camp on the crater rim, with an early start planned for the next day.

days.title: Day 2: Ngorongoro Crater Exploration & Return to Arusha
days.body: Morning: Descend into the Ngorongoro Crater for a half-day game drive on the crater floor, where you may spot the Big Five, along with hippos, zebras, flamingos, and a range of other wildlife in this diverse habitat. Afternoon: After a picnic lunch, begin your journey back to Arusha with memories of an unforgettable crater experience. Evening: Arrive in Arusha for onward travel or departure.

day-tour.title: Day Tour
day-tour.intro: A full-day descent into Ngorongoro Crater from Arusha — one of Africa's most concentrated wildlife arenas in a single unforgettable day.

days.title: DAY 1:Karibu! Safari begins!
days.body: A representative from Aardvark Safaris Tanzania will meet and greet you as soon as you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport and take you to the Mt. Meru Hotel, for your overnight. Arusha, nestled in the shadow of majestic Mount Meru, is a dynamic, fast- growing town and a famed embarkation point for Tanzania safaris. Because of its altitude (roughly 4,600 feet above sea level), Arusha is blessed with a pleasant climate, perfect for the coffee plantations that surround it.

serengeti-southern-migration-zanzibar.title: Serengeti Southern Migration & Zanzibar Beach Holiday
serengeti-southern-migration-zanzibar.intro: Combine the southern Serengeti's calving season and the wild beauty of Nyerere National Park with a relaxing beach extension on the spice island of Zanzibar.
serengeti-southern-migration-zanzibar.route: Arusha · Serengeti Kusini · Namiri · Nyerere · Zanzibar

days.title: DAY 1: Arusha
days.body: Arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, met by your Aardvark representative and transferred to Legendary Lodge for overnight.

days.title: DAY 2: Fly to Serengeti
days.body: Fly into the southern Serengeti. Overnight at Serengeti Kusini, in the heart of the southern shortgrass plains and the calving grounds of the great migration.

days.title: DAYS 3 & 4: Serengeti Kusini
days.body: Two full days exploring the southern Serengeti — vast herds of wildebeest and zebra, attendant predators, and exceptional birdlife on the open plains.

days.title: DAY 5: Drive to East Central Serengeti
days.body: Transfer to East Central Serengeti and check in at Namiri Camp, an area renowned for big cats — particularly cheetah.

days.title: DAY 6: East Central Serengeti
days.body: A full day of game-viewing from Namiri Camp, with lions, leopards and cheetah at the heart of the experience.

days.title: DAY 7: Fly to Nyerere National Park
days.body: Fly south to Nyerere (formerly Selous), Africa's largest game reserve. Overnight at Sand Rivers Lodge on the Rufiji River.

days.title: DAY 8: Nyerere National Park
days.body: Game drives, boat safaris on the Rufiji and walking safaris from Sand Rivers Lodge — Nyerere at its very best.

days.title: ZANZIBAR · DAY 1: Fly to Zanzibar
days.body: Fly across to the spice island. Transfer and overnight at the Hyatt Zanzibar in Stone Town.

days.title: ZANZIBAR · DAY 2: Excursions in Zanzibar
days.body: Spice tour, Stone Town heritage walk, or simply unwind on the turquoise coast. Overnight at Hyatt Zanzibar.

mkomazi-extension.title: Mkomazi National Park Extension
mkomazi-extension.intro: An off-the-beaten-track extension into Mkomazi National Park, home to the Mkomazi Rhino Sanctuary and African Wild Dog reintroduction project — a quiet, uncrowded alternative to Tanzania's famous parks.

days.title: DAY 1: Drive to Mkomazi
days.body: Drive east from Arusha to Mkomazi and begin to experience the wildlife of Mkomazi National Park. Settle into camp this evening.

days.title: DAY 2: Explore Mkomazi National Park
days.body: A full day of exploration and discovery in the park, including a visit to the rhino and wild dog projects. With a small group you'll have great flexibility in what you do.

days.title: DAY 3: Uncharted Territory
days.body: Exploring uncharted territory by day, spotting gerenuk, kudu, and many more game animals.

days.title: DAY 4: Day in Arusha & Departure
days.body: Drive back to Arusha with options for a relaxing day in town before flying out that night.

uganda-extension.title: Uganda Extension — Gorillas, Chimpanzees & Shoebill
uganda-extension.intro: A natural extension to any Tanzania safari: track mountain gorillas in Bwindi, search for the prehistoric Shoebill in Mabamba's papyrus swamps, and trek chimpanzees in the primate capital of the world.
uganda-extension.route: Entebbe · Mabamba · Mbarara · Bwindi · Queen Elizabeth NP · Kampala

days.title: DAY 1: Flight to Uganda
days.body: Met by our Aardvark representative on arrival in Entebbe and transferred to the Lake Victoria Serena Resort, whose gardens of indigenous plants attract butterflies and resident and migratory birds — Splendid Starling, Pied and Woodland Kingfishers, Black-headed Gonolek and more.

days.title: DAY 2: Kampala to Mabamba Bay – Mbarara
days.body: After breakfast, proceed to Mabamba Bay on Lake Victoria where papyrus swamps support over 260 bird species, including the rare Shoebill. Enter the swamps by boat with local guides to look for Shoebill, Palm-nut Vulture, jaçanas, Pygmy Goose, Goliath Heron and more. Continue to Mbarara, arriving in late evening. Igongo Cultural Center Hotel. Transit time 4–5 hours.

days.title: DAY 3: Gorilla Tracking in Bwindi Forest
days.body: An early breakfast and briefing at park HQ, then venture into the steep, often muddy Bwindi forest in search of a habituated group of mountain gorillas. It may take 2–8 hours to reach the gorillas, after which you have a glorious hour of observation and photography. Gorilla tourism provides funds that aid in their conservation.

days.title: DAY 4: Bwindi to Queen Elizabeth National Park
days.body: Drive to Queen Elizabeth National Park, pausing for a short game drive in the Ishasha Sector, well-known for tree-climbing lions. Afternoon boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel — crocs, hippos, waterbucks, Uganda kob, elephants, buffalo, plus flamingoes, herons, ibises, storks, pelicans, the African Fish Eagle and more. Mweya Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 5: Game Drive & Chimpanzee Trekking
days.body: Early game drive on the Kasenyi plains for elephant, leopard, lion, buffalo, warthog and Uganda kob. Afternoon chimpanzee tracking in the Kyambura Gorge — chimps, L'Hoest monkey, black-and-white colobus, red-tailed monkey, olive baboon and more. Mweya Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 6: Return to Kampala
days.body: After breakfast, head back through scenic Uganda countryside to Kampala / Entebbe Airport, with a warm lunch along the way. Connect with international flights or overnight in the area. Transit time 6–7 hours depending on stops.

northern-tanzania-wildlife-safari.title: Northern Tanzania Wildlife Safari
northern-tanzania-wildlife-safari.intro: The Great Migration of the Serengeti is one of the world's most spectacular wildlife phenomena. This safari concentrates on wildlife-rich Tarangire, Serengeti, and Ngorongoro so you spend more time observing and less time travelling — with expert leadership that turns sightings into stories.

days.title: DAY 1: Karibu! Safari begins
days.body: Meet at Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) and transfer to Gran Melia Hotel in Arusha. Nestled below Mount Meru at roughly 4,600 ft, Arusha enjoys a pleasant climate — the classic embarkation point for northern Tanzania safaris.

days.title: DAY 2: Arusha to Tarangire National Park
days.body: After breakfast, drive to Tarangire — in the dry season second only to Ngorongoro for concentrations of wildlife. Permanent water draws elephant, giraffe, wildebeest, zebra, predators, and exceptional birdlife across baobab-studded landscapes. Optional night game drive for nocturnal species.

days.title: DAY 3: Full day in Tarangire
days.body: A full day inside Tarangire National Park. Dinner and overnight at Tarangire Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAYS 4–5: Tarangire to Serengeti National Park
days.body: Three full days in the fabled Serengeti — rolling plains, kopjes, riverine forest, and vast herds. Time to observe behaviour, not just tick species. Your guide enriches every encounter with context on ecology and history. Dinner and overnight at Kubu Kubu Tented Lodge.

days.title: DAY 6: Serengeti to Ngorongoro Highlands
days.body: After an early breakfast, game drive en route to Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Overnight at Lion's Paw on the crater rim.

days.title: DAY 7: Ngorongoro Crater full-day game drive
days.body: Explore one of the world's largest calderas — forests, swamps, grasslands, and lakes supporting lion, cheetah, rhino, elephant, and thousands of antelope. Rare black rhino and big-tusked elephants are highlights. Overnight at Lion's Paw.

days.title: DAY 8: Ngorongoro Highlands to Arusha
days.body: After breakfast, depart for Arusha and Mount Meru Hotel for overnight.

days.title: DAY 9: Departure
days.body: After lunch, transfer to the airport for your onward flight home.

northern-tanzania-wildlife-safari.priceNote: Per person · land safari only (excludes international flights)

uganda-gorillas-chimps-7-day.title: 7-Day Uganda Gorillas & Chimps Trek
uganda-gorillas-chimps-7-day.intro: A primate-rich circuit through Rwanda and Uganda: mountain gorillas in Bwindi (one or two treks), chimpanzees in Queen Elizabeth, tree-climbing lions in Ishasha, and cultural time with Batwa communities — in comfortable 4×4 Land Cruisers with an English-speaking Ugandan guide.
uganda-gorillas-chimps-7-day.route: Kigali · Bwindi · Queen Elizabeth NP · Kigali

days.title: DAY 1: Arrive Kigali
days.body: Welcome at Kigali International Airport, transfer to Kigali Des Mille Collines Hotel overlooking the city. Briefing and warm welcome.

days.title: DAY 2: Kigali to Bwindi
days.body: After breakfast, transfer via the Katuna border to northern Bwindi Impenetrable National Park. Hot lunch en route. Dinner and briefing at Buhoma Community Haven Lodge.

days.title: DAY 3: First gorilla trekking
days.body: Full gorilla trek in Bwindi with park rangers. Certificate on success. Afternoon Batwa community visit — Luke's Batwa Project. Overnight Buhoma Community Haven Lodge.

days.title: DAY 4: Second gorilla trek or birding
days.body: Second trek with a different gorilla family, or optional birding along the Buhoma Valley with a senior local birder. Batwa visit with Joseph's Hope Foundation. Overnight Buhoma Community Haven Lodge.

days.title: DAY 5: Bwindi to Queen Elizabeth NP
days.body: Transfer via Ishasha sector searching for tree-climbing lions. Check in at Park View Safari Lodge. Evening game drive.

days.title: DAY 6: Chimps & Kazinga boat cruise
days.body: Morning chimp tracking in Kyambura Gorge or Kalinzu Forest. Afternoon two-hour boat cruise on Kazinga Channel — hippos, crocs, elephants, and rich birdlife. Park View Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 7: Return to Kigali & depart
days.body: Leisurely breakfast, border formalities, lunch in Kigali, and airport drop-off.

uganda-gorillas-chimps-7-day.priceNote: From per person (dual gorilla trek option) · Kigali start

uganda-holiday-8-day.title: 8-Day Uganda Holiday Tour
uganda-holiday-8-day.intro: A super-luxury Uganda holiday from Entebbe: shoebill birding on Lake Victoria, the Equator, two gorilla treks in Bwindi, tree-climbing lions, chimpanzees, and a sunset boat on the Kazinga Channel — with open-roof 4×4 transport and top-tier lodge accommodation throughout.
uganda-holiday-8-day.route: Entebbe · Mabamba · Bwindi · Queen Elizabeth NP · Entebbe

days.title: DAY 1: Arrive Entebbe
days.body: Meet and greet at Entebbe Airport. Transfer to Lake Victoria Serena Resort (approx. 30 minutes).

days.title: DAY 2: Mabamba shoebill & drive to Mbarara
days.body: Early start for Mabamba shoebill birding by boat. Continue past the Uganda Equator with hot lunch at Equator Coffee Point. Overnight Ingongo Cultural Hotel.

days.title: DAY 3: Drive to Bwindi
days.body: Relaxed breakfast, then drive south to Bwindi. Hot lunch en route. Overnight Silverback Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 4: First gorilla trek
days.body: Early briefing at Buhoma, porter support, full gorilla trekking experience with picnic lunch. Optional afternoon community walk. Silverback Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 5: Second gorilla trek
days.body: Second trek with a different gorilla family group. Picnic lunch and optional community walk. Silverback Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 6: Queen Elizabeth via Ishasha
days.body: Leisurely breakfast, drive through Ishasha for tree-climbing lions and birding. Hot lunch at Mweya Safari Lodge. Optional evening game drive. Overnight Mweya Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 7: Chimps & Kazinga channel
days.body: Light breakfast, chimp tracking in Kalinzu Forest. Afternoon guided boat cruise on Kazinga Channel with birding. Mweya Safari Lodge.

days.title: DAY 8: Return to Entebbe
days.body: Relaxed breakfast and scenic drive to Entebbe for your international departure (domestic flight option available from Mweya).

zanzibar-extension-4-day.title: 4-Day Zanzibar Extension
zanzibar-extension-4-day.intro: The perfect beach finale after a mainland safari: fly from Arusha to Zanzibar for Stone Town heritage, Prison Island tortoises, spice farms, Jozani Forest's red colobus monkeys, and a full day at Mnemba Atoll — with Essque Zalu Beach Resort and Park Hyatt Stone Town.
zanzibar-extension-4-day.route: Arusha · Zanzibar · Stone Town · Mnemba · Departure

days.title: DAY 1: Arusha to Zanzibar & Stone Town
days.body: Fly to Zanzibar. Meet Aardvark representative at Abeid Amani Karume International Airport. Lunch at Park Hyatt, guided Stone Town tour (House of Wonders, Old Fort, Sultan's Palace, markets). Prison Island boat trip for giant Aldabra tortoises. Overnight Essque Zalu Resort.

days.title: DAY 2: Spice tour & Jozani Forest
days.body: Morning spice farm tour — sample fresh cloves, vanilla, and nutmeg. Visit Jozani Forest for rare Zanzibar red colobus monkeys. Sunset stroll on Nungwi Beach. Overnight Essque Zalu Beach Resort.

days.title: DAY 3: Mnemba Atoll
days.body: Full-day excursion to Mnemba Island — snorkel vibrant coral reefs among green turtles, snapper, Moorish idols, and more. Return for dinner at Essque Zalu.

days.title: DAY 4: Departure
days.body: Breakfast and airport transfer for your flight home. Includes one night in Arusha (Olerai Lodge or Mount Meru Hotel) plus airport transfer before the Zanzibar leg.

tanzania.heroDesc: The heart of our operations — Serengeti, Ngorongoro, Kilimanjaro, Tarangire, and Zanzibar.
tanzania.intro: Tanzania offers Africa's greatest concentration of iconic parks on one seamless northern circuit. We craft both luxury tented camps and thoughtfully priced mid-range itineraries, all with private vehicles and expert guides based in Arusha.

parks.name: Serengeti National Park
parks.desc: Vast plains, kopjes, and the Great Migration — wildebeest, zebra, predators, and over 500 bird species.

parks.name: Ngorongoro Crater
parks.desc: The world's largest intact volcanic caldera — black rhino, elephant tuskers, and dense predator populations.

parks.name: Tarangire National Park
parks.desc: Baobab-studded landscapes and one of East Africa's largest elephant concentrations in the dry season.

parks.name: Lake Manyara
parks.desc: Tree-climbing lions, flamingos, and groundwater forest along the Rift Valley escarpment.

parks.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
parks.desc: Summit Africa's highest peak via routes including Northern Circuit, Machame, and Lemosho.

parks.name: Nyerere (Selous)
parks.desc: Boat safaris on the Rufiji, walking safaris, and vast wilderness in southern Tanzania.

wildlife: Calving season on the southern plains

bestTime.note: Peak wildlife viewing; migration in the north; ideal for Kilimanjaro climbs.
Southern Serengeti calving season — predators at their most active.
Fewer crowds, lush scenery, excellent birding and competitive rates.

tiers.desc: Exclusive camps, private guides, charter flights, and bespoke dining — every detail curated for discerning travellers.
Comfortable lodges and tented camps, private 4×4 vehicles, and the same expert guides — exceptional value without compromise on wildlife.

tanzania.circuitsDesc: Tanzania is best understood through its four great safari circuits — each with distinct parks, wildlife, and travel logistics. We design northern, southern, western, and coastal journeys as standalone trips or seamless combinations.

kenya.heroDesc: Maasai Mara, migration crossings, and classic East African savannah.
kenya.intro: Kenya complements any Tanzania itinerary perfectly — especially during the Mara River migration season. We arrange seamless cross-border logistics and camps on both sides of the ecosystem.

parks.name: Masai Mara National Reserve
parks.desc: The migration's dramatic river crossings and year-round big cat action on rolling grasslands.

parks.name: Amboseli National Park
parks.desc: Elephants beneath Kilimanjaro's snow cap — iconic photography and birdlife.

parks.name: Lake Nakuru
parks.desc: Rhino sanctuary, flamingos, and Rift Valley scenery.

parks.name: Samburu
parks.desc: Special five species — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, and arid-adapted wildlife.

culture: Maasai village visits with community partners

bestTime.note: Migration in the Mara; dry season game viewing across the country.
Calving on the short-grass plains; fewer tourists, green landscapes.
Long rains — quiet parks and excellent rates in conservancies.

tiers.desc: Private conservancy camps, exclusive game drives, and fly-in access to remote Mara conservancies.
Comfortable Mara lodges with shared or private vehicles — ideal for families and first-time safari guests.

uganda.heroDesc: Mountain gorillas, chimpanzees, and the Pearl of Africa.
uganda.intro: Uganda is the natural extension to a Tanzania safari — Bwindi's mountain gorillas, Queen Elizabeth's tree-climbing lions, and the prehistoric Shoebill in Mabamba Bay.
uganda.filmDesc: A glimpse of the intimate hour with a habituated family in Bwindi — the experience that draws travellers from Tanzania to the Pearl of Africa.

parks.name: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park
parks.desc: Half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas in misty montane forest.

parks.name: Queen Elizabeth National Park
parks.desc: Kazinga Channel boat cruises, tree-climbing lions in Ishasha, and diverse ecosystems.

parks.name: Kibale Forest
parks.desc: The world's primate capital — chimpanzee trekking and 13 primate species.

parks.name: Murchison Falls
parks.desc: The Nile forced through a narrow gorge — hippos, crocs, and the Shoebill.

bestTime.note: Dry seasons — best trekking conditions in Bwindi and Kibale.
Wetter but fewer permits competition; lush forest photography.

tiers.desc: Boutique lodges, private gorilla trekking arrangements, and charter connections from Tanzania.
Comfortable forest lodges and safari hotels — gorilla permits and ground logistics handled in full.

rwanda.heroDesc: Volcanoes National Park and intimate gorilla encounters.
rwanda.intro: Rwanda offers a compact, polished gorilla-trekking experience in the Virunga volcanoes — easily combined with Tanzania or Uganda for a complete East Africa primate circuit.

parks.name: Volcanoes National Park
parks.desc: Mountain gorilla families on the slopes of the Virungas — Dian Fossey's legacy.

parks.name: Akagera National Park
parks.desc: Savannah restoration success — lion, rhino, and lakeside game drives.

parks.name: Nyungwe Forest
parks.desc: Ancient rainforest — chimpanzees and canopy walkway.

culture: Kigali genocide memorial — powerful historical context

bestTime.note: Dry season — easiest forest trekking and clear volcano views.
Short dry period; excellent for combining with Tanzania safari.

tiers.desc: Volcanoes rim lodges, private guides, and helicopter transfers from Kigali.
Comfortable guesthouses and standard gorilla permit packages with expert trekking briefings.

zanzibar.heroDesc: Stone Town, spice islands, and turquoise Indian Ocean beaches.
zanzibar.intro: After the dust of the savannah, Zanzibar is the perfect finale — dhow sails at sunset, UNESCO Stone Town, and north-coast resorts. We pair beach time seamlessly with your safari flights.

parks.name: Stone Town
parks.desc: UNESCO heritage — Arabian, Persian, Indian, and European architecture and spice markets.

parks.name: Jozani Forest
parks.desc: Endemic red colobus monkeys in the island's only national park.

parks.name: Mnemba Atoll
parks.desc: World-class snorkelling and diving on a protected reef.

parks.name: Prison Island
parks.desc: Giant tortoises and half-day excursions from Stone Town.

culture: Spice farm tours — cloves, vanilla, cinnamon
Taarab music and Forodhani night market

bestTime.note: Cooler, drier — pairs perfectly with peak safari season.
Hot and dry — ideal beach weather after calving-season safari.
Long rains — quieter resorts and lower rates.

tiers.desc: Boutique beach resorts, private villas, and yacht charters off the north coast.
Beautiful beach hotels and heritage stays in Stone Town — the perfect safari add-on.

legal.privacyIntro: Aardvark Safaris Tanzania Ltd respects your privacy. We collect only the information needed to respond to inquiries and plan your safari — such as name, email, phone, and travel preferences.

You may request access or deletion of your data by contacting info@aardvarktanzania.com. privacySections.heading: Information we collect

privacySections.heading: How we use your information
privacySections.body: We use your details solely to respond to enquiries, prepare quotations, confirm bookings, coordinate lodges and park permits, and communicate about your safari. We may send occasional updates about migration seasons or offers if you have opted in.

privacySections.heading: Sharing with third parties
privacySections.body: We share information only with suppliers necessary to operate your trip — accommodation, domestic airlines, ground handlers, Tanzania National Parks, and insurance partners for Flying Doctor evacuation cover. We do not sell or rent personal data to marketers.

privacySections.heading: Retention and your rights
privacySections.body: Booking records are retained as required for accounting and dispute resolution. You may request a copy of your data or ask us to delete non-essential information by emailing info@aardvarktanzania.com. We will respond within a reasonable period.

privacySections.body: Guides and staff may photograph or film safari activities for promotional use. By travelling with us you grant Aardvark Safaris Tanzania Ltd permission to use such material unless you notify us in writing before departure that you do not consent.
